links.scope: All five packaged Windows headless journeys passed. The desktop app and its paired client agreed on whole-plan, first-change, withdrawn and canceled decisions. The independent-window journey checked native focus, separate consent and withdrawal.

links.scope: The Desktop host executes the next approved step from the stored plan. Its receipt and saved system commit together. Tests checked ordered execution, exact repeat under current approval and client access, reopening storage, and revocation before the reply.
limitations: This is local Desktop execution evidence. Managed execution and cross-channel approval need separate checks.

links.scope: The portable client can run one exact approved Desktop step. A separate packaged Windows test created two named systems in order. Pinned transport tests cover lost or invalid replies and exact recovery under current approval without an automatic retry.
limitations: This covers the Desktop step tool and two current UI test inventory rows. It does not qualify managed execution or the full portable workflow.

links.scope: The managed host accepts exact plan proposals over HTTPS. A disposable PostgreSQL test used signed credentials and confirmed the dedicated client could submit and check proposals and use the approved read-only route. Ordinary edits and release approvals were refused. An exact retry kept the first deadline and staging left saved systems unchanged.
limitations: This scope stages and reads proposals. Browser and authenticated chat approval and managed execution still need work.

links.scope: The managed server records whole-plan, individual-change, and withdrawal decisions in the same plan record. A temporary database test used signed test credentials and separate browser documents. The server rejected decisions from stale or expired views. Approval left saved systems unchanged.
limitations: This evidence covers the managed server approval route. The agent still needs to qualify decisions made from authenticated chat and approved changes on the managed server.

links.scope: The built browser app and packaged Windows app passed their approval journeys. The Settings heading stayed in place when the Chrome popup opened. The user could approve the whole plan, approve each change individually, withdraw approval, or close with Escape and return focus to the button. The browser checked that the displayed plan and decision reply matched the request.
limitations: The browser test used a local managed test server. The agent still needs to connect authenticated chat and verify that chat and the app can review the same approval.

links.scope: A test used two connections to a temporary PostgreSQL database. The first connection held the exact synthetic approval record while it checked whether a reply could be sent. A conflicting lock or withdrawn approval prevented the test reply.
limitations: This direct database test used a test administrator. The separate managed execution test used the restricted server role.

links.scope: The official client staged a plan and waited for approval in Chrome. The managed test server saved two approved changes in order. Repeating an exact request returned the saved result and did not create a duplicate. Requests with the wrong client, workspace, revision or step order left saved systems unchanged. After withdrawal, the server refused an exact retry and both saves remained unchanged.
limitations: The live run checked an exact repeat after a normal reply. Separate focused client tests cover a lost or invalid reply.
The agent still needs to connect and qualify authenticated chat approvals.

links.scope: In the signed-in browser, the test approved a whole plan in chat and withdrew it in the popup. A separate plan received its first individual approval in chat and its second in the popup. limitations: This test used the app's approval chat, a local HTTPS server, and a restricted test database role. An external chat client still needs its own way to verify the user or send the user to the matching app popup.

links.scope: The packaged Windows app passed the chat and popup journey with the paired official client. Chat approved a whole plan, which the popup then withdrew.
